title: The little words

example.en: I have a brother and a sister.
I'm not going because I'm ill.
When it rains, I take the metro.
I'm calling to make an appointment.
I don't know if he'll come.
Which bus goes to the centre?
Afterwards we're going to the cinema.
I always have breakfast at home.

words.note: Takes a double negative: Nikdy nekouřím.

example.en: I have a lot of work.

words.note: Takes a double negative: Nic nevím.
Takes a double negative: Nikdo tam není.

example.en: Would you like something to drink?
I take the metro every day.
This week I'm working from home.

words.note: Takes the genitive: u doktora, u okna.
Takes the locative: mluvit o práci.

example.en: After lunch I have a meeting.
I'm waiting in front of the house.
The train leaves in ten minutes.

example.cs: Lékárna je mezi bankou a poštou.
example.en: The pharmacy is between the bank and the post office.
The train is late because of the snow.
What do you do? / What are you doing?

words.note: Takes a double negative: Nikde není.

example.en: I like sport, for example tennis.
I have a letter from mum.
The key is under the doormat.

words.note: Mám svůj klíč. Refers back to the subject.

example.en: I'll call when I get home.
I haven't got a single crown.

example.cs: Byt je hezký, je však drahý.
example.en: The flat is nice; it's expensive, though.
It rained, so we stayed at home.

words.note: Takes a double negative: Nemám žádný čas.

example.en: Shall we meet at, say, five?
It's closed, so we'll go somewhere else.

example.cs: Oba moji bratři bydlí v Brně.
example.en: Both my brothers live in Brno.
I don't understand it at all.
I'm still looking for a flat.

example.cs: Je to jediný obchod v ulici.
example.en: It's the only shop in the street.

example.cs: Je to levné a navíc blízko.

example.en: There are many tourists in Prague.
The others are already at home.
Above all, I'm looking for peace and quiet.
It's not expensive, quite the opposite.
It rained, but we still went out.
I don't have that much money.
Hopefully it will be nice tomorrow.
I won't come: I'm ill, you see.
